adjudication.notes: Paired with T10-capacity-c2.md as Cycle 1 baseline; tentative hiring forecast and platform dependency gaps remain open.

episodes.topic: Status visibility and allocation reporting pain
On-call coverage and team bottleneck management
Workload monitoring boundaries and developer privacy
Sprint commitment predictability and platform dependencies

goals.statement: Engineering leads can independently evaluate sprint progress and team capacity without recurring ad-hoc developer interruptions.

grounding.quote: We really need team leads to be able to assess sprint progress without interrupting developers constantly.

acceptable_paraphrases: Managers can inspect sprint progress without messaging engineers.

goals.statement: Engineering teams maintain dependable production on-call coverage without over-allocating individual engineers.

grounding.quote: we have to maintain dependable on-call coverage without burning out the three people who know the deployment pipeline.

acceptable_paraphrases: On-call rotations remain staffed while distributing workload fairly across engineers.

goals.statement: The capacity planning system avoids tracking individual developer keystrokes, active hours, or surveillance metrics.

grounding.quote: we definitely do not want to track individual keystrokes or active hours, because surveillance destroys engineering trust.

acceptable_paraphrases: System does not monitor personal developer activity or keystroke metrics.

goals.statement: The engineering organization experiences sustained predictability and reduced stress during sprint cycles.

grounding.quote: The whole engineering organization should feel a sense of calm and predictability rather than constant panic.

acceptable_paraphrases: Sprint planning promotes team confidence and psychological comfort.

goals.statement: Team leads detect projected capacity deficits across teams before sprint commitments are finalized.

grounding.quote: Our engineering leads need to detect team overcommitments before sprint kickoff so commitments remain realistic.

acceptable_paraphrases: Identify oversubscribed team workloads prior to sprint start.

goals.statement: Engineering management forecasts quarterly hiring needs directly from historical team velocity deficits.

grounding.quote: maybe we could forecast our quarterly hiring needs from velocity deficits, but we have not agreed on that yet.

acceptable_paraphrases: Estimate future team headcount requirements using past sprint deficits.

traps.note: Priya mentions an Excel sheet with pivot tables as a mental model analogy, not a hard software requirement.
'That bottleneck' in t8 resolves to the unstaffed on-call rotation causing delivery slippage in t6.
Marcus suggests automated background bots inspecting Slack statuses; Priya's hesitant reply must not produce a confirmed goal.
Priya defines a sharp negative boundary rejecting keystroke and active-hour surveillance.

gaps.description: Quarterly hiring forecast goal G6 was proposed tentatively in t8 but never confirmed by stakeholders.
Softgoal G4 (predictability and calm) has only high-level contributors without operational on-call mitigation.

entailment_cases.hypothesis: Engineering managers require capacity visibility without having to disrupt individual engineers repeatedly.
The capacity planning system must be built as an Excel spreadsheet workbook with embedded Visual Basic pivot tables.
The system records developer keystrokes and browser tab activity to calculate utilization percentages.
All engineering tasks must be estimated using Fibonacci planning poker cards led by certified scrum masters.
